posts.title: Open weights vs hosted APIs
posts.text:
I spent three days debugging vLLM thread locks just to save $400 on API costs.

Open weights are only cheaper until you pay a senior engineer $250k to babysit the inference stack at 3 AM.

Managed APIs are just paying the intelligence tax so you can sleep. Disagree?

posts.title: AI coding tools
posts.text: I watched a junior developer ship a 400-line cursor-generated PR that looked pristine, except it silently caught every database exception and returned HTTP 200. AI coding tools are amazing at syntax and entirely lethal to context.

posts.title: Observability for LLMs
posts.text:
I watched a junior dev try to debug a looping agent with `console.log` today and aged three years.

If you aren't logging exact token counts, prompt hashes, and model endpoints, you aren't debugging—you're just guessing in prod.

Most "LLM observability" startups are just overpri

posts.title: RAG is not a search box
posts.text:
I spent three days debugging a hallucinating agent before realizing the LLM wasn't wrong, my top-k retrieval was just pulling garbage paragraphs.

Fixing your chunking strategy beats spending $2,000 fine-tuning a bigger model every single time.

posts.title: Evals before demos
posts.text:
I spent yesterday watching a team rewrite their system prompt three times because the founder "vibed" with a demo.

If your test set is just the founder's group chat, you aren't building AI, you're doing expensive theater.

Write 50 evals before you touch the UI.

posts.title: Prompt injection
posts.text:
I spent yesterday watching an agent scrape a support ticket and happily execute a curl command to an external webhook because a user hid `rm -rf` inside a CSS style tag.

Prompt injection isn't a security bug. It's just the fundamental cost of letting text execute code.

posts.title: Benchmark contamination
posts.text:
I stopped trusting public eval charts the day I watched a model ace a benchmark it had memorized word-for-word in its pre-training dump.

Your next model isn't smarter; the test set just leaked into the weights.

Unseen data is the only eval that matters.

posts.title: Hiring for AI teams
posts.text:
I spent three hours tracing a phantom hallucination in a RAG pipeline only to find the prompt was fine and the embedding model just drifted.

The bottleneck isn't prompt engineering anymore. It's debugging non-deterministic memory leaks at 3 AM.

Agree or disagree?

posts.title: Fine-tuning vs prompting
posts.text:
I watched a team spend three weeks curating a fine-tuning dataset of 40 examples only to see their hallucination rate double on edge cases.

Fixing the system prompt and dropping to a smaller quantized model cut their p99 latency in half and actually solved the drift.

posts.title: Latency budget
posts.text:
I spent yesterday ripping out a 450-token local draft model because it added a 1.2s pause on every cursor stop.

Users prefer a dumb, instant autocomplete over a genius model that makes them wait for the UI to breathe. Latency is a feature.

Agree or disagree?

posts.title: Token pricing race
posts.text:
I spent the morning refactoring an agent loop because we hardcoded context windows assuming $0.10 input tokens.

The race to zero inference cost is making us build architectural debt disguised as clever prompt engineering.

Smart routing will matter more than raw price cuts. Agre

posts.title: Vibe coding vs shipping
posts.text:
I watched an LLM hallucinate an entire Stripe webhook handler at 2 AM last week. Vibe coding your prototype is fine until a database migration drops your production users table.

Writing actual backend code isn't the bottleneck anymore. Debugging it is.

posts.title: Reasoning models cost
posts.text:
I watched a 40-second reasoning loop turn a $0.002 API call into a $0.18 timeout error in staging today.

Letting a model think until it hits max tokens isn't intelligence, it's just an expensive infinite while-loop.

Timeout budgets should be enforced in code, not left to the vi

posts.title: AI agents in production
posts.text:
I watched an autonomous agent loop on a 429 rate limit for three hours until it ran up a $400 API bill.

Your demo works because the happy path is easy. Production fails on retries, OAuth token expiration, and partial database writes.

posts.title: Cheap models vs frontier models
posts.text:
I routed our JSON extraction pipeline to a $0.20/M model and watched the retry loop burn three times the compute fixing bad syntax.

Frontier models aren't expensive because of the output token. They're cheap because they stop your agent from looping itself to death.

posts.title: Model routing
posts.text:
I watched a team burn $14k in a week routing simple JSON extraction to Claude 3.5 Sonnet.

Hardcoding your biggest model for every prompt isn't rigor, it's just an expensive form of laziness.

Router logic beats raw weights every single time.

posts.title: Vector database hype
posts.text:
I migrated our search off a dedicated vector db last week and saved $800/mo on memory alone. Turns out most apps just needed a smarter chunking script and a BGE reranker over SQLite.

You don't have a vector scaling problem. You have a preprocessing problem.

posts.title: The 10x engineer myth
posts.text:
I watched an engineer generate 4,000 lines of boilerplate with Claude yesterday and spend six hours debugging a memory leak because they didn't know how Rust lifetimes worked.

AI just exposes who can actually architect.

posts.title: Goodbye Claude, Hello Pi
posts.text:
I migrated my core agent loop off Claude this morning because the latency tax on simple tool routing is just too high for local state management.

For routine JSON parsing, paying enterprise weights is dead money.
